WHAT’S HAPPENING

“Do something about this while I’m gone.”

That’s what his wife said at the front door before she left for six weeks with her sisters. Mike knew what she meant. Somewhere in the last few years he’d disappeared: the gut came in and never left, the stairs left him breathless, and he was done by the afternoon and asleep in the chair with the TV on.

So he did everything he was supposed to. Cut the beer. Cut the bread. Salad every night. Walked every morning before work. Took the stairs instead of the lift. Two weeks later the scale hadn’t moved. Not one pound.

WHAT’S REALLY GOING ON

“It’s your arteries.”

So Mike went to the one guy who might know: Rafael, 54, a trainer who never seems to slow down. Mike listed everything. The belly. The soft arms. The stairs. The afternoon crash. Waking at 3 a.m.

Rafael’s answer: as you age, artery walls stiffen and the pipes narrow, so blood can’t move the way it used to. And every part of you runs on that blood: your muscles, your brain, your heart. When delivery slows, everything slows at once.
